findings.sourceEvidence: §7.8(m)(i): "(i) interest rate Swap Agreements in the ordinary course of business up to an aggregate notional principal amount not to exceed at any time an amount equal to the Commitments of all the Lenders in the aggregate at such time,"
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The rule's action is "OTHER" with no operator or qualifier limiting it to interest rate swaps; the only captured condition is "in the ordinary course of business," and the capacity expression is a plain reference to the "Commitments" term. Nothing in the rule carries the word "interest rate."
findings.verifierReasoning: The source exception carves out only "interest rate Swap Agreements." The instrument defines "Swap" broadly (any agreement constituting a swap under CEA §1a(47)), so absent the "interest rate" qualifier the proposed IR's permission is materially wider than the source: it would authorize a currency, commodity, or credit swap in the ordinary course within the cap, whereas §7.8(m)(i) authorizes only interest rate swaps. Constructed test: a commodity swap that constitutes an Investment. Under the source it is not within the (m)(i) exception (only interest rate swaps are carved out), so it is caught by §7.8's general prohibition on Investments (unless another exception applies). Under the proposed IR, that commodity swap would be treated as permitted (in ordinary course, within the Commitments cap). A downstream reviewer applying the proposed IR would therefore conclude broader swap capacity exists than the source actually grants. The proposed IR marks its own sufficiency as COMPLETE, and this broadening is precisely the kind of confident-but-wrong overstatement that warrants specific scrutiny.

findings.sourceEvidence: §7.8(m) header: "(m) to the extent constituting Investments, any"
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The proposed IR presents (m)(i) as a free-standing PERMISSION with no representation that the carve-out operates only "to the extent constituting Investments," and no representation of the underlying §7.8 prohibition it is excepted from.
findings.verifierReasoning: The (m) header conditions the carve-out on the activity constituting an Investment, i.e., the exception operates within §7.8's prohibition on Investments. The proposed IR omits both that qualifier and the underlying prohibition. This does not change any real conclusion on its own: Swap Agreements that do not constitute Investments were never restricted by §7.8 and needed no carve-out, while Swap Agreements that do constitute Investments are covered by the exception in either reading. The omission is therefore non-material considered alone (it does not, for instance, cure or worsen the interest-rate overstatement captured in the first finding).
